# Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair

Last updated: 30 October 2026

> An independently owned Priceline Pharmacy franchise store on the ground floor of Pacific Fair Shopping Centre, Broadbeach, open 7 days. Scripts ready in minutes, walk-in vaccinations, pharmacist consultations and beauty advice, with the GPs of Help Medical, an independent general practice located inside our store.

## Key facts
- Vaccinations (ages 5 and over): Free for eligible people under the National Immunisation Program, with no service fee.
- Vaccines: COVID-19 vaccines are free only for eligible groups since 1 October 2026 (75+, 65–74, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people 50–74, adults 18–64 with severe immunocompromise). Rabies, dengue, yellow fever and polio vaccines are not offered in store; we refer to a GP or travel clinic.
- Medication packing (Webster packs): Free for concession and health care card holders. $5 a week otherwise.
- Ear piercing (ages 8 and over): $65 for both ears, including earrings and an antiseptic aftercare spray. Walk in. Second holes in the earlobe are fine; sleepers and other earrings are sold in store. No nose piercing; call first about cartilage.
- Passport and visa photos: $25. About 10 minutes.
- Contraception consultation: $35 consultation. Your contraception is charged separately; ask us about the cost of your option. Please call first; trained pharmacists are usually available Monday to Friday.
- UTI treatment: No booking needed. Walk in. For women aged 18 to 65 with symptoms of an uncomplicated bladder infection.
- Sick leave certificates: pharmacists issue absence from work certificates (personal or carer’s leave) for minor, short-term illnesses they can assess. Walk in on the day; certificates can’t be backdated; a consultation fee applies. Some universities and TAFE courses don’t accept pharmacist certificates for assessments.
- Parking: 4 hours of free parking at Pacific Fair each day.
- Delivery: Everyday health, beauty and wellbeing products delivered through Uber Eats. Prescription medicines can’t be delivered this way.
- Send scripts ahead: email the eScript link or QR code to pharmacy@pricelinepf.com.au (checked throughout the day while the store is open), or send it through MedAdvisor or the Priceline Pharmacy app. Paper prescriptions must be brought in.
- Prescription wait: most scripts are ready in 5 minutes or less, sometimes 5 to 10 minutes, rarely longer. A robotic dispensary picks medicines, and extra dispensary staff are rostered so patients still get counselling about their medicine. Names are called when a script is ready; customers who step out can come back to the prescription counter and give their name to check progress.
- Full scripts: the pharmacy supplies the full quantity on a prescription, not part of it; if stock is short, customers are told when they hand the script in and can have it ordered in or take it elsewhere.
- Stock checks: customers can call (07) 5592 2099 or email pharmacy@pricelinepf.com.au to check a medicine is in stock before coming in.
- Early repeats: often possible for regular medicines such as blood pressure and cholesterol medicines; some medicines can’t be supplied early without the doctor’s approval. For people who are travelling, the pharmacy is happy to try calling their doctor for approval.
- Paper scripts held at another pharmacy (for example, visitors on holiday): that pharmacy can email (pharmacy@pricelinepf.com.au) or fax ((07) 5504 6612) a copy and post the original; the medicine can usually be supplied from the copy.
- Private consultation room: available for private conversations with a pharmacist; no appointment needed.
- Returns: the store follows Priceline’s Returns and Exchange Policy. Faulty products: refund or exchange under the Australian Consumer Law. Change of mind: within 30 days with proof of purchase, for unopened, unused items in original sealed packaging. Excluded from change-of-mind returns: prescription, Pharmacist Only and Pharmacy Only medicines, vitamins and supplements, infant formula, consumables such as food, gift cards, and products with less than 3 months to expiry.
- Fragrance: every fragrance sold is genuine; testers are available in store, and fragrance can be sprayed on a testing card to take home.
- Payment: Afterpay is available at the till in store.
- Sharps: used needles, syringes and lancets can be dropped off in a sealed sharps container for safe disposal.
- Compounding: the pharmacy does not compound (specially make) medicines; compounded prescriptions need a compounding pharmacy.
- Late night: open until 9pm on Thursdays.
- Quietest time: weekdays, 8am to 10am (walk-ins are welcome any time).
- Help Medical: An independent general practice located inside our store, with a QML Pathology collection room open Monday to Friday, 8:00am – 1:00pm. Closed weekends.

- Address: Shop 81, Pacific Fair Shopping Centre, Hooker Blvd, Broadbeach QLD 4218
- Phone: (07) 5592 2099
- Email: info@pricelinepf.com.au (general), pharmacy@pricelinepf.com.au (prescriptions)
- Opening hours: Monday to Wednesday: 8am – 5:30pm; Thursday: 8am – 9pm; Friday: 8am – 5:30pm; Saturday: 9am – 5:30pm; Sunday: 9:30am – 4:30pm. Open on every Queensland public holiday except Christmas Day, Good Friday and Anzac Day; public holiday hours vary and are published on the Google Business Profile (dates: https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/public-holiday-hours/).
- Overseas visitors: most international cards accepted, including UnionPay (for Alipay, check at the counter). GST can usually be claimed back through the Tourist Refund Scheme on purchases of AU$300 or more (GST included) made within 60 days of leaving Australia. Buying vitamins in bulk? Contact us before you visit: we may be able to offer a discount and help arrange postage. Staff speak English and use a translation app.
- Christmas and New Year hours: Fri 27 Nov (Black Friday) 8am – 7pm; Fri 18 Dec 8am – 7pm; Sat 19 Dec 9am – 7pm; Sun 20 Dec 9am – 6pm; Mon 21 Dec 8am – 9pm; Tue 22 Dec 8am – 9pm; Wed 23 Dec 8am – midnight; Thu 24 Dec (Christmas Eve) 8am – 6pm; Fri 25 Dec (Christmas Day) Closed; Sat 26 Dec (Boxing Day) 8am – 6pm; Sun 27 Dec 9am – 6pm; Mon 28 Dec (public holiday) 10am – 5pm; Tue 29 Dec 8am – 5:30pm; Wed 30 Dec 8am – 5:30pm; Thu 31 Dec (New Year’s Eve) 8am – 9pm; Fri 1 Jan (New Year’s Day) 10am – 5pm.
- Google rating: 4.6 from 164 Google reviews (checked 29 October 2026). A selection of reviews: https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/reviews/
- Owner and pharmacist: Jason Markey, BPharmSci, MPharm, Ahpra registration PHA0001976405. Independently owned Priceline Pharmacy franchise store, opened 2009.
- Every advice article is reviewed by Jason Markey before it's published: https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/about-us/jason-markey/ (how we write and check articles: https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/editorial-policy/)
- Book online: https://app.medadvisor.com.au/Network/PRICELINEPHARMACYPACIFICFAIR
- Help Medical (independent general practice inside the store): (07) 5619 3818, website https://helpmedical.au/, online bookings https://www.hotdoc.com.au/medical-centres/broadbeach-QLD-4218/help-medical/doctors. Hours: Monday to Wednesday: 8am – 5pm; Thursday: 8am – 9pm; Friday: 8am – 5pm; Saturday and Sunday: 9:30am – 4pm.
- QML Pathology collection inside Help Medical: Monday to Friday, 8:00am – 1:00pm. Closed weekends.

## Services
- [Prescriptions & eScripts](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/prescriptions/): Paper scripts, eScripts, Active Script Lists, hospital, interstate and vet scripts. Send yours ahead.
- [Vaccinations](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/vaccination-information/): Flu, COVID-19, whooping cough, shingles, RSV, pneumococcal and travel vaccines. Walk in or book.
- [Flu vaccination](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/flu-vaccination/): Yearly flu shot, walk in or book. Free for eligible people under the NIP.
- [Whooping cough vaccine](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/whooping-cough-vaccine/): Whooping cough booster for ages 5 and over, walk in or book. Free in pregnancy under the NIP.
- [Travel health & vaccinations](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/travel-health/): Travel vaccines, a travel health kit and advice on taking your medicines overseas.
- [Medication packing (Webster packs)](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/medication-packing/): Your medicines sorted by day and time in weekly blister packs.
- [Medication reviews](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/medication-reviews/): A free one-on-one check of all your medicines with a pharmacist.
- [Free health checks](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/health-station/): Free blood pressure, heart rate, weight, BMI, body fat and diabetes risk checks, by SiSU Health.
- [Diabetes & NDSS](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/national-diabetes-services-scheme/): Blood glucose monitors, test strips and Libre sensors, plus subsidised NDSS supplies.
- [Weight management support](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/weight-loss-counselling-and-advice/): Free, private one-on-one support to lose weight or manage your weight, with free progress checks.
- [Delivery](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/delivery/): Health and beauty products delivered across the Gold Coast via Uber Eats.
- [Click & Collect](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/click-and-collect/): Shop online at priceline.com.au and collect from us, usually within 15 minutes.
- [Priceline Pharmacy app](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/download-the-priceline-app/): Order scripts ahead, get reminders and manage your Pulse Rewards.
- [Contraception consultations](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/contraception-consultations/): Start, change or continue your contraception with a trained pharmacist. $35.
- [UTI treatment](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/uti-treatment/): Assessment and treatment for uncomplicated bladder infections, women 18 to 65.
- [Sick leave certificates](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/sick-leave-certificates/): Absence from work certificates for minor, short-term illnesses, after a private chat with a pharmacist.
- [Emergency contraception](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/emergency-contraception/): No appointment or consultation fee. Fill in a short private questionnaire and a pharmacist checks what’s suitable.
- [Women's health](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/womens-health/): Contraception, UTI treatment, pregnancy, periods and menopause support from our pharmacists.
- [Quit smoking & nicotine dependence](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/quit-smoking/): Free help to quit smoking and manage nicotine dependence: a plan, NRT advice and follow-up.
- [Passport & visa photos](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/passport-photos/): Australian and overseas passport and visa photos while you wait. $25.
- [Ear piercing](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/ear-piercings/): Both ears, with earrings and antiseptic spray included. $65, walk in.
- [Skincare & self-tan](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/skincare-tanning/): Free advice from trained beauty advisors, and brands that suit the Gold Coast climate.
- [Makeup & fragrance](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/beauty-fragrance/): Makeup, fragrance, dental care and men’s grooming with help from our beauty team.
- [Perfume & fragrance gifts](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/fragrance/): Designer and celebrity fragrance with testers in store, and free help choosing a scent or gift.
- [Vitamins & supplements](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/vitamins-supplements/): Everyday and practitioner ranges, checked against your medicines by a pharmacist.
- [Metagenics](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/metagenics-vitamins/): Practitioner-range supplements in stock or ordered in, with pharmacist advice.
- [Help Medical GPs](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/help-medical/): An independent general practice located inside our store. Bulk billing for everyone with a Medicare card, QML pathology collection, walk-ins welcome.
- [Blood tests (QML Pathology)](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/blood-tests/): QML Pathology collection room inside Help Medical, in our store. Walk in with your request form, weekday mornings.

- [How to get rid of old medicines safely (free at the pharmacy)](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/how-to-dispose-of-old-medicines/): Unwanted medicines go back to any pharmacy for free, safe disposal. What we accept at our Pacific Fair counter, where sharps go, and how to read expiry dates.
- [How to help an ageing parent manage their medicines](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/help-elderly-parent-with-medication/): Visiting Mum or Dad over the holidays? How to help an elderly parent with medication: warning signs, medicines lists, packs, reviews and safe disposal.
- [How to move your prescriptions to a new pharmacy](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/transfer-prescriptions-new-pharmacy/): Moving scripts to a new pharmacy is free. How to bring across eScripts, your Active Script List, paper repeats and your PBS Safety Net record, step by step.
- [PBS Safety Net 2026: thresholds, tracking and what you pay after](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/pbs-safety-net-explained/): In 2026 the PBS Safety Net is $1,748.20 for general patients and $277.20 with a concession card. How to count family scripts, and what you pay after.
- [What can a pharmacist treat in Queensland without a GP?](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/what-can-a-pharmacist-treat-queensland/): Trained Queensland pharmacists can treat UTIs, offer contraception consultations and help with reflux, ear infections, school sores, eczema, acne and shingles.
- [Why your pharmacist asks questions (and sometimes for ID)](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/why-pharmacists-ask-questions/): How medicines are grouped in Australia, why pharmacists ask who it's for, why some cold and flu tablets need photo ID, and the rules on early repeats.

### Vaccinations
- [Flu season in Queensland: when to get your flu shot](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/when-to-get-flu-shot-queensland/): When to get your flu shot in Queensland before the winter peak, who may get it free, side effects and what to expect. Walk-in flu shots at Pacific Fair.
- [Free vaccines at the pharmacy in Queensland: who's eligible in 2026](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/free-vaccines-pharmacy-queensland/): Which vaccines are free at a Queensland pharmacy in 2026: flu, COVID-19, RSV, shingles, pneumococcal, catch-ups and more, who qualifies and what changed.
- [Shingles vaccine: who can get it free and why it matters](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/shingles-vaccine-free/): The shingles vaccine is free under the NIP from 65, from 50 for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and for some immunocompromised adults.
- [Vaccines for uni students: placements, colleges and catch-ups](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/vaccines-for-uni-students/): Starting uni? Which vaccines health students need before clinical placements, why college students need meningococcal vaccines, and which catch-ups are free.
- [Whooping cough vaccine in pregnancy: what you need to know](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/whooping-cough-vaccine-pregnancy/): Recommended in every pregnancy, ideally at 20 to 32 weeks, so antibodies reach your baby before birth. Whether it's free, and why partners and carers matter.

### Travel health
- [Do you need vaccinations for Japan? What Australians should know](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/japan-vaccinations/): Most trips to Japan need no special vaccines, but check measles and flu, ask about Japanese encephalitis for rural stays, and know Japan's medicine rules.
- [Passport photo requirements: Australia and common visa sizes](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/passport-photo-requirements/): Australian passport photo rules (35–40mm by 45–50mm, plain background, no glasses), guarantor endorsement, and photo sizes for US, UK, China and more.
- [Travel health checklist: what to sort 6–8 weeks before you fly](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/travel-health-checklist/): Our travel health checklist counts down from 8 weeks to the day before you fly: vaccines, scripts, PBS rules and a travel kit, sorted at Pacific Fair.
- [Vaccinations for Bali: what Australians need before they go](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/bali-vaccinations/): No vaccines are needed to enter Bali, but measles, hepatitis A and typhoid are worth having. When rabies and JE vaccines make sense, and avoiding Bali belly.
- [Vaccinations for China: what Australians need before they go](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/china-vaccinations/): China needs no entry vaccines, but check measles, flu, hepatitis A and typhoid. Extra advice for family visits, altitude in Tibet and live animal markets.
- [Vaccinations for Fiji: what Australians need before they go](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/fiji-vaccinations/): Fiji has no malaria and is rabies-free, but dengue and leptospirosis after floods are risks. The vaccines to check, from measles to typhoid, and food safety.
- [Vaccinations for India: what Australians need before they go](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/india-vaccinations/): Most travellers to India need hepatitis A and typhoid vaccines. Why visiting family raises your risk, rabies and JE advice, and a fake rabies vaccine alert.
- [Vaccinations for Thailand and Vietnam: a pharmacist's guide](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/thailand-vietnam-vaccinations/): Hepatitis A for most trips, typhoid especially for Vietnam or street food, and when rabies and JE vaccines make sense. Start 6 to 8 weeks before you fly.

### Vitamins & supplements
- [Magnesium supplements: which type, and what the evidence says](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/magnesium-supplements-guide/): Citrate, chloride and lactate forms absorb better than magnesium oxide. The evidence for cramps and sleep, who runs low, and which medicines to space it from.
- [Should you take a probiotic with antibiotics?](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/probiotics-and-antibiotics/): Some probiotic strains may reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhoea, but not every product has been studied. Timing, choosing a strain and who should avoid them.
- [Supplements that can interact with your medicines](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/supplements-that-interact-with-medicines/): St John's wort with antidepressants and the pill, vitamin K with some blood thinners, minerals with some antibiotics: supplement interactions and staying safe.
- [Vitamin D on the Gold Coast: do you still need a supplement?](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/vitamin-d-gold-coast/): Most Gold Coast locals get enough vitamin D from everyday sun. Who still runs low, how to balance sun and skin cancer risk, testing, and supplement doses.

### Dental & oral care
- [Dry mouth: common causes (including medicines) and what helps](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/dry-mouth-causes-relief/): About 600 medicines can cause dry mouth, including antidepressants and antihistamines. Why it matters for your teeth, and what helps if a medicine is the cause.
- [Electric vs manual toothbrush: which is better?](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/electric-vs-manual-toothbrush/): A Cochrane review of 56 trials found powered brushes cut plaque and gingivitis more, but technique matters most. Who benefits and which features are worth it.
- [Mouth ulcer treatment: home care and when to worry](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/mouth-ulcer-treatment/): Mouth ulcer (mouth sore) treatment: saltwater rinses, soft foods, numbing and protective gels from the pharmacy, and when to see a Gold Coast dentist or GP.
- [Teeth whitening strips and kits: are they safe?](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/teeth-whitening-safety/): Home whitening kits in Australia are limited to lower peroxide strengths, but sensitivity and gum burns still happen. Who should see a dentist first.

### Baby & child
- [Gastro in kids: how to keep them hydrated and when to worry](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/gastro-in-kids-hydration/): Small sips often, even if they're vomiting: using oral rehydration solution (frozen into ice blocks), signs of dehydration and Queensland childcare rules.
- [Paracetamol and ibuprofen for kids: doses, timing and safety](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/childrens-paracetamol-ibuprofen/): Dose by weight, not age: how often to give children's paracetamol and ibuprofen, the daily limits, who shouldn't have ibuprofen, and whether to give both.
- [Sun protection for babies: what's safe under 12 months](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/baby-sun-protection/): Queensland's UV Index is 3 or above all year, so babies need shade, clothing and hats. Why sunscreen waits until 6 months, and how to cover a pram safely.
- [Threadworms: how to treat the whole family and stop reinfection](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/threadworms-treatment/): Treat everyone in the house at once, even people without symptoms, and usually repeat in one to two weeks. The hygiene steps that stop eggs reinfecting you.

### Hair & scalp
- [Dandruff treatment: your questions answered](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/dandruff-treatment/): Dandruff treatment explained: causes, medicated shampoos, home tips and when to see a GP. Handy advice for Gold Coast swimmers who wash their hair often.
- [Head lice: how to get rid of them (and stop them coming back)](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/head-lice-treatment/): Treat, then treat again: conditioner and a lice comb every 2 to 3 days, or a lotion repeated after 7 days. Why lice come back, the myths, and school rules.
- [Postpartum hair loss: why it happens and when it stops](https://pricelinepacificfair.com.au/postpartum-hair-loss/): Shedding often starts two to three months after birth and usually settles on its own. Why it happens, what's normal, supplements, and when to see a GP.
